cas:100-42-5.note: A colorless liquid chemical used mainly to make plastics and rubber, such as polystyrene. It is also found in some foods, such as cinnamon.

cas:10124-43-3.note: A salt of the metal cobalt. It is used in pigments, electroplating and batteries, and as a source of cobalt in animal feed.

cas:107-06-2.note: An industrial liquid, also called 1,2-dichloroethane, used mainly to make vinyl chloride for PVC plastic.

cas:107-30-2.note: An industrial chemical used to make other chemicals, such as ion-exchange resins.
cas:107-30-2.caveat: The listing covers technical-grade chloromethyl methyl ether, grouped with the related chemical bis(chloromethyl) ether.

cas:117-81-7.note: A plasticiser, also called DEHP, used to make PVC plastic soft and flexible, for example in tubing, flooring and packaging.

cas:1314-20-1.note: An oxide of thorium, a radioactive metal. It was used in gas lamp mantles, special glass and an old medical imaging agent.
cas:1314-20-1.caveat: Listed under ionizing radiation: the concern is the radiation given off by thorium.

cas:14464-46-1.note: A crystalline form of silica (silicon dioxide) that forms at high temperatures. It occurs in some volcanic rocks and in heat-treated diatomaceous earth.
cas:14464-46-1.caveat: Listed for breathing in fine crystalline silica dust, mainly in workplaces. The listing does not describe silica in other forms.

cas:14808-60-7.note: A crystalline form of silica (silicon dioxide) and the main mineral in most sand. It is used to make glass and ceramics.
cas:14808-60-7.caveat: Listed for breathing in fine crystalline silica dust, mainly in workplaces. The listing does not describe silica in other forms.

cas:15347-57-6.note: A salt of the metal lead. It has been used in some hair dyes that darken grey hair gradually, and in dyeing and printing fabrics.
cas:15347-57-6.caveat: Listed as part of lead and lead compounds as a group.

cas:15468-32-3.note: A crystalline form of silica (silicon dioxide) that forms at high temperatures. It occurs in some volcanic rocks.
cas:15468-32-3.caveat: Listed for breathing in fine crystalline silica dust, mainly in workplaces. The listing does not describe silica in other forms.

cas:2475-45-8.note: A blue synthetic dye that has been used in hair dyes and to colour fabrics and plastics.

cas:25013-16-5.note: Butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA) is a synthetic antioxidant added to fats, oils, foods and cosmetics to slow them from going rancid.

cas:298-81-7.note: A compound found in some plants, used as a medicine together with ultraviolet A light to treat skin conditions such as psoriasis.
cas:298-81-7.caveat: Listed for its use as a medicine taken together with ultraviolet A light treatment.

cas:302-01-2.note: A reactive industrial chemical used as rocket fuel, to remove oxygen from boiler water, and to make foaming agents, farm chemicals and medicines.

cas:3296-90-0.note: A chemical containing bromine, used as a flame retardant in plastics such as unsaturated polyester resins.
cas:3296-90-0.caveat: Listed for the technical-grade product, a less purified commercial form.

cas:50-00-0.note: A simple chemical, a gas at room temperature, used to make resins for wood products and as a preservative. It also forms in the body and occurs in many foods.

cas:50-28-2.note: The main female sex hormone, made in the body and also made for medicines such as hormone therapy.
cas:50-28-2.caveat: Listed as part of steroidal estrogens, mainly for their use as medicines.

cas:542-75-6.note: A liquid soil fumigant used on farms before planting to control nematodes, tiny worms that damage crop roots.
cas:542-75-6.caveat: Listed for the technical-grade product, a less purified commercial form.

cas:57-63-6.note: A synthetic form of estrogen, a female sex hormone, used mainly in birth control pills.
cas:57-63-6.caveat: Listed as part of steroidal estrogens, mainly for their use as medicines.

cas:57-83-0.note: A female sex hormone made in the body, also made for medicines used in pregnancy support, hormone therapy and birth control.

cas:62-44-2.note: A pain and fever medicine, used in the past and since withdrawn in many countries. It has also been used as a stabiliser in some products.

cas:62-56-6.note: An organic compound containing sulfur, used in photographic processing, textile finishing, metal cleaners and making resins.

cas:67-66-3.note: A dense, sweet-smelling liquid used mainly to make refrigerant chemicals. It also forms when chlorine is used to treat water.

cas:71-43-2.note: A colorless liquid made mainly from crude oil, used to make plastics, resins, nylon and other chemicals. It is also present in gasoline and tobacco smoke.

cas:7440-02-0.note: A silvery metal used in stainless steel and other alloys, coins, plating and batteries. It is also used as a catalyst to harden vegetable oils.

cas:7446-34-6.note: A compound of selenium and sulfur, used mainly in anti-dandruff shampoos and in medicated treatments for scalp and skin.
cas:7446-34-6.caveat: The listing is based on studies of selenium sulfide taken in by mouth, not shampoo use.

cas:75-01-4.note: A gas used mainly to make PVC plastic. Small leftover amounts can remain in PVC products.

cas:75-07-0.note: A simple organic chemical found in ripe fruit, coffee and bread, which also forms in the body when alcohol is broken down. It is used as a flavoring.

cas:75-09-2.note: A solvent, also called dichloromethane, used in paint strippers and degreasers, and to remove caffeine from coffee and extract flavors from spices.

cas:75-21-8.note: A gas used to sterilize medical equipment, to fumigate spices in some countries, and to make other chemicals such as antifreeze and detergents.

cas:75-52-5.note: An industrial liquid used as a solvent, in making other chemicals, and as a fuel in racing engines and model engines.

cas:75-56-9.note: A reactive liquid used mainly to make polyurethane plastics and propylene glycol, and as a fumigant for some nuts and spices.

cas:7646-79-9.note: A salt of the metal cobalt, also called cobalt chloride. It is used in humidity indicators that turn from blue to pink when damp, and to make other cobalt compounds.

cas:7664-93-9.note: A strong mineral acid used widely in industry, including fertilizer making and car batteries. It is also used in food processing to adjust acidity.
cas:7664-93-9.caveat: Listed for breathing in strong acid mists, mainly in workplaces. The listing does not describe sulfuric acid used to adjust acidity in food.

cas:77-09-8.note: A chemical used as an acid-base indicator in laboratories and formerly as a laxative medicine.

cas:79-01-6.note: A chlorinated solvent used mainly to remove grease from metal parts, and to make refrigerant chemicals.

cas:8007-45-2.note: A thick dark liquid made from coal. It has been used in medicated shampoos and skin treatments for dandruff and psoriasis, and in road and roof tar.

cas:93-15-2.note: Also called methyleugenol, a compound found in basil, tarragon, nutmeg and other herbs and spices, and in some essential oils.

cas:94-59-7.note: A compound found in sassafras oil and in nutmeg and some other spices. It was once used to flavor root beer.
